text.p: Following are some major events to have occurred on August 14 in history:
1040 - King Duncan of Scotland was murdered by Macbeth, who then became king and ruled for 17 years.
1385 - Portuguese forces thwarted an attempted invasion by John I of Castille at the battle of Aljubarrota, securing independence for the Portuguese.
1551 - Turkish forces captured Tripoli, Libya.
1678 - William of Orange attacked the French army near Mons. The French, caught by surprise, rallied and repulsed William who lost several thousand men.
1742 - Pius VII, Pope from 1800-23, born. He was imprisoned by Napoleon 1809-14; he later restored the Jesuit order.
1778 - Augustus Toplady, English hymn-writer who wrote "Rock of Ages", died.
1840 - Baron Richard Krafft-Ebbing, German neurologist noted for his studies of forensic psychiatry and sexual deviations, born.
1893 - France became the first country to introduce motor vehicle registration plates.
1900 - The Boxer Rebellion, a peasant uprising aimed at forcing all foreigners from China, was finally defeated when an international force captured Beijing.
1908 - World's first international beauty contest was held at the Pier Hippodrome at Folkestone, England.
1912 - U.S. Marines landed in Nicaragua to protect American interests there.
1920 - King Albert of Belgium opened the seventh Olympic Games in Antwerp.
1935 - The Social Security Act, establishing old age benefits and unemployment insurance, was passed by the U.S. Congress.
1941 - The Atlantic Charter was signed by U.S. President Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Churchill. The charter was later included in the United Nations Declaration.
1945 - Japan accepted the Allies' terms of unconditional surrender, ending World War Two.
1949 - Konrad Adenauer was appointed first chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany.
1951 - William Randolph Hearst, U.S. newspaper owner and publisher, died. Orson Welles's film "Citizen Kane" caused controversy as it appeared to be based on the life of Hearst, a power in Hollywood.
1962 - After three and a half years of digging, Italian and French workers completed the road tunnel under Mont Blanc, when the last three metres (nine feet) separating the two sides was dynamited.
1970 - Yugoslavia and the Vatican announced the resumption of full diplomatic relations after an 18-year break.
1971 - Bahrain declared itself a fully independent and sovereign state.
1972 - A Soviet Ilyushin 62 exploded after takeoff from Schoenefeld Airport, East Berlin, killing all 156 aboard.
1974 - Fighting resumed in Cyprus after peace talks in Geneva broke down over a Turkish demand for autonomous regions on the island.
1984 - J. B. Priestley, English novelist and playwright, died. Best known for the novel "The Good Companions" and plays such as "An Inspector Calls".
1986 - Riots broke out across Pakistan against the government of President Zia; three people were shot dead and opposition leader Benazir Bhutto was arrested.
1987 - A Sri Lankan soldier in a guard of honour for visiting Indian Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi broke ranks and struck him with his rifle butt.
1988 - Enzo Ferrari, Italian racing pioneer and sports car builder, died at his home in Modena aged 90.
1989 - P.W. Botha resigned as South African president.
1992 - Judge John Sirica, a central figure in the Watergate scandal, died. He ordered President Nixon to hand over his White House tapes.
1996 - The National Party, the architects of South African apartheid, moved to the opposition benches for the first time in 48 years.
1996 - Gambian military leader Captain Yahya Jammeh lifted a two-year ban on political parties, telling them to prepare for a presidential election in less than a month.
1996 - Romanian-born Sergiu Celibidache, one of the world's most celebrated orchestral conductors, died. He was principal conductor of the Munich Philharmonic.
